clue.text: Well, these French, joints carry 16s

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the vessels that do the carrying; 16 is 16-down, space travellers

parts.note: a spa is a spring or well of mineral water
ces is French for these
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: A tourist at a French watering-place mentions the ailing joints the waters are meant to help.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 16 sends you to 16-down, so the definition means craft that carry space travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels built for travel beyond the atmosphere are what carry crews of space travellers.

clue.text: This changed since being out of date

indicators.note: changed says the four letters of This are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes this has changed as it has gone out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out of date' tells you the word is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sith is an old form meaning from the time when, used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Breathless greeting heard in the plant

indicators.note: heard signals that the greeting is spoken and a word with the same sound is written

parts.note: hallo with its aspirate h dropped, 'allo

explanation.surface: A gasped hello is heard in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathless' means without breath, the aspirated h, so hallo becomes 'allo. 'plant' could be a factory; it is the succulent.
explanation.definitionFit: The aloe is a succulent plant with fleshy leaves.

clue.text: How Mark Twain described his obituary notice

definitions.text: How Mark Twain described his obituary notice

parts.words: How Mark Twain described his obituary notice
parts.note: Twain said reports of his death were greatly overstated, describing the premature notice

explanation.surface: A note on what the humorist said of his own death notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain called the report of his death 'an exaggeration'; overstatement is the sense.

clue.text: Henrietta not drinking in the country dance …

indicators.note: in tells you one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the hey is an old country dance
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A sober woman sits out the country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hetty is a pet form of the name Henrietta.

clue.text: … so sanctimonious rake takes her, not Henry, up for a spin

annotationWithheld.why: … so sanctimonious rake takes her, not Henry, up for a spin (9): PI + ROUE then needs TTE, but HETTY (4d, 'her') less H reversed gives YTTE; no reading of the held clue gives TTE
annotationWithheld.clue: … so sanctimonious rake takes her, not Henry, up for a spin

clue.text: Bright fish mouthing surprise and contempt ?

parts.note: O is a cry of surprise
pah is an exclamation of contempt

explanation.surface: A gaudy fish seems to gape in astonishment and scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouthing' is a link: the fish mouths two exclamations.
explanation.definitionFit: The opah, or moonfish, is a large, brilliantly coloured ocean fish.

clue.text: ' Mountain climbing ", one article in Mill's material he's stolen

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word goes upwards, read back

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

indicators.note: in puts the two pieces inside the miller's material

parts.note: grist is grain for grinding at the mill
I is the Roman numeral one
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the title of a passage in John Stuart Mill's work was lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mill' suggests the philosopher; it is a flour mill. 'he's stolen' is loose: the man who has stolen others' writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who passes off another's writing as their own has stolen it.

clue.text: Sam roughed out Dad's line of defence

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the two words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Sam drafts a defence plan for his father.
explanation.walkthrough: In wartime Britain the Home Guard was manned by older men, later nicknamed Dad's Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Guard was Britain's volunteer force of older men, the last line of defence.

clue.text: Mama showing craft

parts.note: the word is MA written twice, and MA is the abbreviation for the arts degree held by a graduate of some standing

explanation.surface: Mother displays her handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Mama reads as two MAs, and an MA is a Master of Arts. 'craft' looks like skill; it is a vessel with two masts.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing vessel with a pair of masts is a kind of craft, meaning a boat.

clue.text: It's soothing, translating Lamb

indicators.note: translating turns the word into different form, so the letters of Lamb are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds Charles Lamb's essays a calming read in another language.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm is an ointment or remedy that soothes.

clue.text: Passage where a pin-up could be a failure

definitions.text: Passage where a pin-up could be a failure

parts.words: Passage where a pin-up could be a failure
parts.note: a long alley for bowling at pins; a pin left standing up means the throw failed

explanation.surface: An alley where a pin-up picture is a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A skittle alley is the long lane on which balls are bowled at skittles.

clue.text: Poor starter plainly finishes in higher feather

definitions.text: Poor starter plainly finishes in higher feather

parts.words: Poor starter plainly finishes in higher feather
parts.note: the fairy tale of a plain, unpromising chick that grows into a fine swan: a poor start, finishing in grander plumage

explanation.surface: A racehorse or athlete starts badly but finishes in fine form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in higher feather' plays on 'in fine feather' (in good form) and on the swan's plumage; 'plainly' is the bird's plain looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen's tale is of a scorned cygnet that turns out to be a swan.

clue.text: On which a begging letter may start fireworks ?

definitions.text: On which a begging letter may start fireworks ?

parts.words: On which a begging letter may start fireworks ?
parts.note: a request for money is a touch, and a letter is written on paper; the same term is the fuse paper lit on a firework

explanation.surface: A request for money might cause an explosion of anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' is slang for asking someone for money, and 'fireworks' also means an angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch-paper is the slow-burning paper lit to set off a firework.

clue.text: Iris's 18 disturbed PE class

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are moved out of their order

parts.note: the name with its possessive S counted as a letter
18 is 18-across, the heavenly blazer

explanation.surface: Iris's gym class is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the possessive S of Iris's is used as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometrics are exercises in which muscles push against resistance, a form of physical education.

clue.text: Outside broadcast employee taking notice

parts.note: a servant is an employee

explanation.surface: A member of the outside-broadcast crew pays attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and alert means noticing what goes on.

clue.text: " North star, out " a trip for him ?

definitions.text: " North star, out " a trip for him ?

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, the letters tripping over one another into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller heads out past the Pole Star on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller makes a trip out among the stars.

clue.text: A fish-eater, namely, of 'igher degree?

parts.note: a fish-eating animal whose name, said with a dropped h, sounds like hotter, 'of higher degree'; the clue wants that animal's famous name

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks about a fish-eater of superior rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is an otter, and ''otter' is 'hotter' with the h dropped, so of higher degree (temperature). Tarka the Otter is Henry Williamson's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarka is the named otter hero of Henry Williamson's 1927 novel.

clue.text: Calphurnia's heavenly blazer

parts.note: in Julius Caesar, Calpurnia says the heavens themselves blaze forth the death of princes; a heavenly blazer is a body that blazes across the sky

explanation.surface: Caesar's wife sports a smart jacket fit for heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blazer' looks like a jacket; it is something that blazes. Calpurnia's line begins 'When beggars die, there are no comets seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A celestial body with a blazing tail is the sky-sign Calpurnia speaks of.

clue.text: 26 thus trained on the crossbars

parts.note: 26 is 26-across, a garden flower; one grown up a lattice of crossbars is trained that way

explanation.surface: A climbing flower is trained up a wooden frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant fixed to a lattice of crossed laths is supported on a garden frame.

clue.text: Morbid sort of science

definitions.meaning: morbid in the sense of diseased, or obsessive to an unhealthy degree
relating to the study of disease

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a branch of science as gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the study of disease: unhealthily compulsive, and relating to that medical science.

clue.text: Accustom Yorkshiremen to swim here

definitions.meaning: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Get Yorkshire folk used to bathing in their own river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, so a local might swim in Ure.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to harden someone to something by habit.

clue.text: Heady snares for those drying out in saloons

definitions.text: Heady snares for those drying out in saloons

parts.words: Heady snares for those drying out in saloons
parts.note: snares worn on the head, used in hairdressing saloons while customers dry

explanation.surface: Intoxicating traps lie in wait for drinkers trying to give up in bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drying out' suggests giving up drink and 'saloons' bars; they are hairdressing salons where wet hair dries.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine nets hold a hairstyle in place while it dries.

clue.text: See 22
Moralist has lost his grip somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way, an anagram

explanation.surface: A preacher has lost his hold on his audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-righteous, priggish person lectures others on morals.

clue.text: Make-up for a writer in silly game .

indicators.note: in places a and the writing implement inside the jumbled letters
silly suggests the letters of game are muddled

parts.note: a quill is a pen, something that writes

explanation.surface: A writer is given a role in a frivolous game of dressing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests an author; it is the pen. 'silly' makes MAGE from GAME, and 'in' puts A QUILL after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Maquillage is the French-derived word for cosmetics.

clue.text: … got up for a girl

definitions.meaning: past tense of rise, got out of bed
a girl's name, also a flower

explanation.surface: A young woman got out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to 25: the make-up was for a girl who got up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is both the past tense of rise and a common female name.

clue.text: Purloin, you say, CID's weighing machines?

indicators.note: you say signals the word for purloin is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to purloin is to steal
the CID is part of Scotland Yard, the Yard, so CID's gives Yard's

explanation.surface: A detective asks whether the police scales have been pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the London police, based at Scotland Yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is a balance with a sliding weight on a long arm.
